### 1. What the user expresses; simulator behaviour

- Target: cash out "as much of your earnings as you can to that debit card right now" (simulator opening line). The card is the bank debit card ending 8427, "the one you put on last week", which she gives only when asked.
- Timing: now (Friday 2026-10-02).
- Boundary of action: cash out to the debit card. She says nothing about the plan, the bounced payout or anything else ("you do not suggest anything else that might need doing").
- Authorisation: she gives open consent for anything that needs sorting on the payout account ("whenever the agent explains that something needs sorting out on your account, you simply say that is fine and to go ahead"). She runs the cashout herself, with exactly the account number, amount and fee the agent gives her. If asked which plan she wants, she says she wants to cash out instantly to the debit card and not use the Cartwise card.
- The simulator only states her need, answers passively (DOB on the identity check; the card; the plan; "frozen for about a week and then being told it was cleared" if asked why a payout bounced) and runs the user tool when it is handed over. It does not steer the procedure.

Act now. Visible eligibility grounds:

### 4. Scored parameters (formula, inputs, tier, value)

**(a) Re-send of the returned transfer** (resend_returned_payout_amount_terms and the resend factor documents)
- Baseline: amount still to re-send = latest returned-transfer entry 208.00 less re-send deposits pointing to it (none) = 208.00. It is sent "in full … with nothing set off or kept back". **Fall-back answer: 208.00.**
- Re-send limit, recent destination (resend_limit_recent_destination): the destination was replaced 2026-09-24, 8 days ago (<30), and the account was verified 2023-04-14, 41 whole months ago (≥12) → at most 150.00. Found from the payout account record (destination_changed_at, verified_date).
- Standing scale (resend_limit_standing_scale): Full-Service Shopper Gold with 48 base-pay entries in the last 3 months (≥24) → limit ×1.25 = 187.50. Found from the contractor account level and Cartwise Shopper Batches base-pay rows.
- Amount drawn = min(208.00, 187.50) = 187.50.
- Clawback reserve (resend_clawback_reserve_notes): 1 batch pay reversal in the last 12 months (2026-08-11) → 10.00. Found from the batch pay-reversal row.
- Conduct hold (resend_conduct_hold_schedule): 2 active violation points (1–5) → 10.00. Found from violation_points_balance on the contractor account.
- Earnings debit set-off (resend_earnings_debit_setoff): exactly 1 returned-transfer entry in the last 12 months, shopper below Diamond (Gold) → the most recently booked earnings debit, 6.40 (2026-09-25). Found from the payout entries.
- Re-send = 187.50 − 10.00 − 10.00 − 6.40 = **161.10**, answering returned_event_id de39653f-b054-4138-9089-c6786157a13d.
- The holds are "taken off the amount drawn" (clawback, set-off), and the conduct hold example reads "90.00 drawn … leaving 65.00". So the limit is applied first and the holds are subtracted from the amount drawn.

**(b) Catch-up deposit** (catchup_deposit_amount_rule and the catch-up factor documents), worked after the re-send
- Balance after the re-send is 458.90 (tool receipt). Baseline: balance less every credit of the unfinalized batch = 458.90 − 45.60 = 413.30, dated with the end of the latest closed weekly earnings period, 2026-09-27. **Fall-back answer: 413.30.**
- New-destination limit (catchup_new_destination_limit): replaced 8 days ago (<30), verified 41 whole months ago (≥12) → at most the largest single weekly sweep deposit ever booked, re-sends not counted = 226.10 (2026-09-15). Clause 2: "The catch-up deposit draws on the smaller of the balance on the account and the limit" → draws on min(458.90, 226.10) = 226.10.
- Leave-behind for the unfinalized batch (catchup_unfinalized_batch_leave_behind): Gold or above with 48 base-pay entries in the last 3 months (≥24) → only the tips posted on that batch, 11.00 (in place of every credit, 45.60).
- Conduct buffer (catchup_conduct_buffer): 2 points → 12.00.
- Tip-reduction buffer (catchup_tip_reduction_buffer): 1 tip reduction in the last 3 months (2026-09-25) → 7.50.
- Returned part (catchup_returned_part_treatment): 208.00 − 161.10 (the re-send now pointing to it) = 46.90. There is exactly 1 returned-transfer entry in the last 12 months and the shopper is Gold (Gold or below) → half kept = 23.45.
- Catch-up = 226.10 − 11.00 − 12.00 − 7.50 − 23.45 = **172.15**, payout_period_end **2026-09-27**.
- Residual reading risk (recorded, not resolved by me): the limit document says the deposit "draws on" the smaller of the balance and the limit, and the other catch-up factors describe amounts that "stay on the balance and [are] not part of the catch-up deposit". A reader could instead cap the finished figure: min(226.10, 458.90 − 11.00 − 12.00 − 7.50 − 23.45 = 404.95) = 226.10. I chose 172.15 because clause 2 makes the limit the figure the deposit draws on, which puts it in place of "the balance" in the baseline, as the resend documents do explicitly ("taken off the amount drawn"). The catch-up documents do not say so as explicitly as the resend documents do.

**(d) Debit-card cashout** (debit_cashout_amount_terms and the debit factor documents), worked after (a)–(c)
- Balance after the catch-up is 286.75 (receipt). Plan Instant Cashout: fee 0.50, largest single cashout 500.00, daily total 500.00, nothing cashed out today.
- Baseline: 286.75 − 11.00 tips − 0.50 fee = 275.25; lowest of 275.25/500/500 → 275.25 with fee 0.50. **Fall-back answer: 275.25 (fee 0.50).**
- Fee (debit_cashout_fee_schedule): Gold, no instant cashout in the last 3 months → half of 0.50 = **0.25**.
- Tips held (debit_cashout_unfinalized_tip_hold): Gold with exactly 1 tip reduction in the last 6 months (2026-09-25) → line 2 (Silver or above, exactly one) → half of 11.00 = 5.50.
- Conduct hold (debit_cashout_conduct_hold): 2 points → 8.00.
- Earnings-debit buffer (debit_cashout_earnings_debit_buffer): 2 earnings debits in the last 3 months (08-11, 09-25) → 7.50.

- Competing visible text (recorded): facet_instant_cashout_fees_and_limits note 4 says "on Instant Cashout that cashout [the first instant cashout after verification] carries a fee of 0.00 and later cashouts carry 0.50". The ledger visible from 2026-07 shows no instant cashout, and nothing visible shows whether one was ever made since verification in 2023. payout_instant_cashout_rules clause 8 declares retired the clause that booked "0.00 for the first cashout after verification where the plan waived the fee", and says the waiver "remain[s] a figure of each plan". So I did not apply the waiver, and took the fee from the in-force fee schedule (0.25). A reader who trusts facet note 4 would pass fee 0.00 and amount 217.07. See the kb findings below.

### 6. Problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

Root: the debit-card instant cashout (customer's own write, user tool).

- **Hop 1 — root waits on plan = Instant Cashout (state-derived).** debit_cashout_desk_card: "> An instant cashout to an external debit card is worked out only after the account's payout plan on record is Instant Cashout." find_payout_accounts shows variant_name "Everyday Pay Card Platinum", so the state does not hold. I searched for the write that makes the plan on record "Instant Cashout" using the words "payout plan", "Instant Cashout" and "external debit card". card_plan_exit_move_off_card says an account on an EPC plan "may move to a plan without a card … a shopper who now receives payouts to an external debit card moves to Instant Cashout" and "The account's payout plan on record becomes the plan moved to". The destination on record (8427, changed 2026-09-24 on a confirmed change_destination request) is the external debit card the customer names. Result: move off the card plan to Instant Cashout, with its cashback settlement. Condition "allowed only while the payout account is active" holds.
- **Hop 2 — root waits on a catch-up deposit (state-derived).** debit_cashout_desk_card: "> An instant cashout is not worked out until the account carries a catch-up deposit covering the weekly deposit days that passed while the account was not active." Records: no weekly deposit for the period ending 2026-09-27, a return on 09-23 that froze the account (R1), and the account active now. So a weekly deposit day passed while not active, and no catch-up deposit is booked, so the state does not hold. catchup_deposit_desk_reference describes the write that brings it about ("For those days the company sends a single catch-up deposit once the account is active again … Once booked, the account carries a catch-up deposit covering the weekly deposit days that passed while the account was not active"). These are the same words as the sentence.
- **Hop 3 — catch-up waits on a re-send deposit pointing to the latest returned transfer (state-derived).** catchup_deposit_desk_reference: "A catch-up deposit is fixed only after the latest returned-transfer entry on the account has a re-send deposit pointing to it." Records: the latest returned-transfer entry de39653f (208.00) has no re-send pointing to it. resend_returned_payout_desk_reference: "the returned amount is sent again at once as its own re-send deposit, which points to the returned-transfer entry it answers". The conditions "new destination on file after a transfer came back" (09-24 after 09-23) and "account is active again" hold.
- The re-send and the move off the card carry no prerequisite sentence of their own in the visible corpus. A statement payment was also checked: 2026-09 is still waiting (entries booked 10-01, 1 day < 4), and the cashback due = 74.60 − 74.60 = 0.00 < 1.00, so none is owed. The move-off-card documents carry no waiting sentence in any case.
- Dependency direction and order: re-send → catch-up → cashout; move off card → cashout; the move is independent of re-send and catch-up.
- Hop marks: all three state-derived. None pre-solved: no document names another problem's tool, and no route or aggregated chain was used.

### Two-way counter-proof

- "Do only what the customer asked for" (hand over the debit cashout at once): excluded by the two visible prerequisite sentences on the debit desk card, whose states are false on the records (plan EPC Platinum; no catch-up deposit). Handing it over now leaves the governed amount not yet workable under the visible rule.
- Cash out onto the Everyday Pay Card instead (cash_out_to_card): excluded because the customer wants her bank debit card (she answers "rather than use the Cartwise card" if asked), and because the move rule sends a debit-card destination to Instant Cashout.
- Move to Weekly Direct Deposit instead of Instant Cashout: excluded because that plan is for a bank account destination, offers no instant cashouts (tariff "No"), and the destination is a debit card.
- Catch-up before the re-send: excluded by the catch-up timing sentence. The returned part treated in the catch-up also depends on the re-send already booked (46.90 half-kept 23.45 versus 208.00 half-kept 104.00).
- Two catch-up deposits (one per period): excluded by "One catch-up deposit covers every earnings period…". The period end is 2026-09-27, the latest closed period (the Sunday before the frozen Friday), not 2026-10-04 (not closed) and not 2026-09-20 (already swept and returned).
- Statement month for the exit settlement 2026-08: excluded because it already carries a payment (09-05). The latest month with earned entries is 2026-09.
- Fall-back numbers (baseline only): re-send 208.00, catch-up 413.30, settlement 60.00, cashout 275.25 with fee 0.50. Each differs from the answer reached (161.10, 172.15, 71.56, 216.82 with 0.25). Every factor document was reached from the record's own words: "pay reversal" (batch events), "violation points" (contractor account), "earnings debit" (payout entries), "destination changed"/"verified" (payout account), "base pay"/"mileage"/"heavy pay" (batch pay components), "Cartwise+ Annual" (membership), "plan_changed_date" and "activated_date". None of the computation documents I read says that a variation exists or that certain customers qualify for something else. The resend baseline's "with nothing set off or kept back" is noted for the dependency-form scan.
- Residual alternatives recorded above: catch-up 226.10 (limit applied to the finished figure), and fee 0.00 / amount 217.07 (first-cashout waiver read from facet note 4).

Residual readings recorded blind, checked against the source:
- Catch-up assembly: the source rule states "The catch-up first takes the smaller of the balance and the catch-up limit, then subtracts what is left behind for the unfinalized batch, the returned part kept, the tip-reduction buffer and the catch-up conduct buffer". The compute is `MN(dep_limit, bal) - held - kept - tip_buffer - conduct_buffer`. That is the reading I chose. The visible carriage is catchup_new_destination_limit Clause 2 ("The catch-up deposit draws on the smaller of the balance on the account and the limit in Clause 1") together with (c) "otherwise it draws on the whole balance" and the baseline "the balance on the account less …". Together these put the limit in the position of "the balance", which entails the source order. The alternative (cap the finished figure, 226.10) is not supported by any visible sentence, so it is not an equally reasonable formula. It is recorded as a wording-strength observation in policy_kb/0.md, not as a runtime failure.
- Fee 0.00 via facet note 4: the source retires the base clause that booked "0.00 for the first cashout after verification" (payout_ext_debit_cashout overwrite on payout_evt_instant_cashout). The fee is decided by the debit_cashout_fee ladder (0.25). The facet note comes from the source's own parameter gloss (`instant_fee_waiver_first_cashout: whether the first instant cashout after verification is free`). The visible corpus adjudicates the conflict through payout_instant_cashout_rules clause 8. This is recorded as a policy-side note in policy_kb/0.md.
- Freeze window evidence: prerequisite_closure confirms "the lift leaves no dated record". The unmet catch-up state is carried by the missing 2026-09-29 deposit, the 09-23 return and R1/W2, which is what the blind answer used. It is visible and derivable.

Contamination: the pre-audit glance at blueprint/products/payout.yaml lines 1–30 (binding and lifecycle) touched none of the compared items.

Verdict: **KB-RUNTIME PASS**. From the visible materials alone, every hop was state-derived. All four written values, the ids, the plan, the statement month, the period end, the owners and the order equal the source-layer solution. No visible text forces waiting or refusal. No hidden field was needed.
